# LocalizationService

- Inherits [`Instance`](instance.md)
- A **service**: get it with `game:GetService("LocalizationService")`
- **Not creatable**: it cannot be created with `Instance.new`

Returns the game's text by key, in the player's language. A project has one catalog per locale, such as `i18n/en.json` and `i18n/pt-BR.json`, each a flat JSON object that maps keys to text. A script asks for a key: `Translate("menu.play")`.

A key is looked up in the player's locale, then in the project's default locale, then in the engine's own text. If none has it, the key itself is returned and a warning is logged once.

Text properties are plain strings and are not translated automatically. A label shows the string it was given; a game that changes language at run time sets its labels again when `LocaleChanged` fires.

The language is a player setting, like the graphics settings. It is not saved with a scene and is not replicated. On a dedicated server, which has no player, `Translate` returns the text of the default locale, and setting `Locale` raises an error.

This page lists the members this class declares. Inherited members are
listed on the page of the class that declares them.

## Properties

| Name | Type | Default | Access | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Locale` | `string` | `"en"` | read/write | The locale that text is returned in, such as `en` or `pt-BR`. Setting it records the player's choice: the choice is kept for the next run, and `LocaleChanged` fires.<br><br>The initial value is the first of these that exists: the player's saved choice, the language of the store or launcher that started the game if a platform provider reports one, the system language, `[project] default_locale`, and `en`. Each is matched to a catalog the project has.<br><br>A locale the project has no catalog for is matched to a catalog of the same language, so `pt` uses `pt-BR`. If there is none, setting it raises an error. |
| `VoiceFollowsLocale` | `boolean` | — | read-only | Whether the voice language follows the text language. It is true until a language is set on `VoiceLocale`, and true again after `VoiceLocale` is set to an empty string. A settings menu can use it to show "same as text" as the current choice. |
| `VoiceLocale` | `string` | `"en"` | read/write | The language that voices are played in, which can differ from the language of the text. When a `Sound` is played, its `Content` is looked for under `l10n/<VoiceLocale>/`. Reading this property returns the language in effect, which is always one of `GetVoiceLocales`.<br><br>Set to an empty string, the default, it follows the text language: `Locale` matched to a language this machine has voices for, or else the first system language it has voices for, or else the project's default. `VoiceFollowsLocale` reports whether it is following.<br><br>Setting a language records the player's choice, which is kept for the next run. A language this machine cannot play is matched to one of the same language, so `pt` uses `pt-BR`; if there is none, setting it raises an error. A change takes effect at the next `Play`: a sound that is playing finishes in the language it started in. |

## Methods

### `GetLocales(): { string }`

Returns the locales the project has a catalog for, in order. Use it to fill a language menu.

### `GetSystemLocales(): { string }`

Returns the system's preferred languages, most preferred first, as the platform reports them, whether or not the game supports them. Use it to show "your system's language" in a menu. Returns an empty list on a dedicated server.

### `GetVoiceLocales(): { string }`

Returns the languages this machine can play voices in, with the project's default first and the others sorted. The others are the languages under `l10n/` that the game shipped with or that an installed language pack added. A menu built from the list never offers a voice language that is not installed.

### `Translate(key: string, arguments: { [string]: any }?): string`

Returns the text for `key` in the current `Locale`. Each `{name}` in the text is replaced by `arguments.name`, which can be a string, a number or a boolean. If no catalog has the key, the key itself is returned and a warning is logged once.

## Events

Signals are deferred: a handler runs at the next resumption point, not
inside the call that fired the signal.

### `LocaleChanged(locale: string)`

Fires when `Locale` changes. During development, it also fires when a catalog file is edited and reloaded. Set the text of the game's labels in its handler.

### `VoiceLocaleChanged(locale: string)`

Fires when the language that voices are played in changes, with the new `locale`. That happens when a script sets `VoiceLocale`, or when the text language changes and the voice language follows it.
